newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger, focus on election.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger, focus on election.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Monday, taking their direction mostly from gains in U.S. Treasuries, with investors looking ahead to results of today's federal election.

"It's mostly following the U.S. But today is a monster coupon day," said Jim Webber, head of fixed-income research with TD Securities. "Investors do have some cash to play with. For a lot of people it's a question of whether you wait until you're absolutely certain what's happening in the election."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.43 to C$112.53 to yield 6.995 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 8/32 to yield 6.89 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 11 basis points from 12 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

Both Canadian and U.S. bonds opened stronger following the release of weaker-than-expected economic data in both countries. U.S. Treasuries were helped by a report showing consumer spending edged up at its slowest rate in seven months during April.
In Canada, the key data out this morning was a report showing real gross domestic product grew by a lower-than-expected 0.8 percent in the first quarter.

The Canadian data did not have a major impact on bond prices because investors remain focused on the outcome of today's federal election, Webber said. While the governing Liberal party has a commanding lead in the polls, the main issue for many traders is whether the party will maintain its majority.
With some C$4.7 billion in coupon payments falling due today, Webber said there was adequate cash available for investors to put to work, but many may be waiting to see the outcome of the election.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.15 to C$105.61 to yield 6.478 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.63 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds was 15 basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.97 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 4.95 percent.
